events.fact: Slack apps are created and managed via the developer portal at https://api.slack.com/apps.
To distribute a Slack app to other workspaces, developers must configure an OAuth 2.0 flow and activate Public Distribution under the Manage Distribution section of the app dashboard.
Submitting an app to the Slack Marketplace requires the app to be fully functional, publicly available, and installed on 10 or more active workspaces (used in the past 28 days) before submission.

The Slack Marketplace review process consists of a preliminary review (taking up to 10 business days for feedback) and a functional review (taking up to 10 weeks for new submissions, or 6 weeks for updates).

Unlisted distributed apps do not require Slack Marketplace approval and can be installed via shareable installation URLs and OAuth flows immediately, but workspaces with 'Require apps from Slack Marketplace' or 'Require approved apps' enabled will block or require admin approval for unlisted apps unless configured otherwise.

Slack OAuth 2.0 authorize endpoint is https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize (or OpenID Connect authorize at https://slack.com/openid/connect/authorize) and token endpoint is https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access.

events.fact: Slack API rate limits apply per method per app per workspace, divided into Tier 1 (1+ req/min), Tier 2 (20+ req/min), Tier 3 (50+ req/min), Tier 4 (100+ req/min), and Special limits (such as 1 msg/sec for chat.postMessage). Exceeding limits returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After.
Slack supports PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for public clients and authorization code flows.

Installing via OAuth authorization code flow involves redirecting users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with client_id, scope, and redirect_uri, then exchanging the authorization code via POST to https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access.
